candidate.answerReason: The two roots simplify to sqrt(3) and 3sqrt(3)/2. Their difference is -sqrt(3)/2, whose square is 3/4.

methods.label: Simplify the roots before squaring
methods.explanation:
Simplify both roots first, because they become multiples of the same square root. All roots here denote their nonnegative values. The sixth root is the one-sixth power, so, using \(27=3^3\),
\[
\sqrt[6]{27}=(3^3)^{1/6}=3^{3/6}=\sqrt3.
\]
Also, the mixed number \(6\frac34\) equals \(\frac{27}{4}\). Factoring \(27=9\cdot3\) lets us take the square roots of \(9\) and \(4\):
\[
\sqrt{6\frac34}=\sqrt{\frac{27}{4}}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Now combine the like radical terms before squaring:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(\sqrt3-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2
&=\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{3}{4}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac34}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
